FIX_FIRST for F1: the aggregate budget charges only the sources of each evaluation, so step repeat amplifies a small hostile document past it (about 2^18 retained elements per layer, uncharged), which is the exact V4-02 case the budget exists for. The fix is one line plus new test numbers, and should land before the one bundled run. F2 (a moved or scaled layer can store a non-finite free distort corner that serialises to null and bricks the vector entry) is a cheap guard. F3 adds two suites to the bundled run, because the ruling-Q4 command rows reach harness-core and the harness typed-row sweep. F4 is the builder's envelope finding: a correct finding, with a small fix that fits the lane (see envelope_order_ruling). F5 and F6 are low and the lead may waive them. Item 5's exporter wait is honestly named.

findings.severity: unsafe: unbounded aggregate allocation (V4-02); a hostile document of about 1 MiB can exhaust memory in render and export
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-composite/src/vector_live_filters.rs:116-128 (evaluate_stack charges `elements` of `current` before evaluate at :121-123, never the output); module doc :20-22 and the composite DESCRIPTOR limits row ('source elements ... charged before each evaluation'); nib live_effect/laws.rs:496-500 (step repeat admits (copies+1) x per_copy <= MAX_OP_ELEMENTS 2^18 per evaluation); composite src/vector.rs:2099 and :2136 (prepare_vectors keeps every layer's VectorLayerSpec in `specs` until prepare_vector_layers); expand_vectors :2528-2541 (each fill row clones `base`)
findings.what: A layer's last evaluation output is never charged, and step repeat turns a tiny source into up to 2^18 elements. The aggregate budget therefore bounds what the stacks read, not what they allocate and retain. One layer with a 5-element rectangle and one step repeat of 43689 copies is charged 5 elements and keeps about 218k elements. Every layer of the call does the same, and prepare_vectors holds all specs at once (stroke outlines of them too). The lane notes and the DESCRIPTOR claim that many layers 'cannot multiply nib's per-evaluation limit', and that does not hold for outputs. Both budget tests use twists (output = input) or copies 0, so they cannot see it.
findings.scenario: A document with 1000 vector layers (well inside folio's default Budget.nodes 4096 and the 1 MiB input budget), each a 5-element rectangle with one stack entry {filter_kind step_repeat, copies 43689, move_horizontal 0}: (43689+1) x 6 = 262140 <= 2^18, so nib admits every evaluation. composite charges 1000 x 5 = 5000 of the 4194304 budget. prepare_vectors then holds about 1000 x 218450 = 2.2e8 path elements (GBs at tens of bytes per element, plus their stroke outlines) before prepare_vector_layers runs, and expand clones them per fill row. The result is an allocation abort, not a vector_effect_work_limit refusal. The element size is UNVERIFIED; the counts are READ.
findings.fix: In evaluate_stack, after `current = evaluate(..)?`, also charge the output: `let out_elements = current.iter().map(|p| p.elements.len() as u64).fold(0, u64::saturating_add); *budget = budget.checked_sub(out_elements).ok_or(REFUSE_EFFECT_WORK)?;` (per evaluation the over-allocation before the refusal stays under nib's 2^18). Alternatively, charge the initial sources once and then every output. Update both budget tests (with in+out charging the copies-0 chain fits 8, not 16; the 4096-twist case fits 1638 layers) and add one red test: many layers each with a large-copy step repeat over a small rect, expecting vector_effect_work_limit past the budget. Fix the doc line, the DESCRIPTOR limits row and the lane notes.

findings.certainty: READ (code path); serde_json writing null for a non-finite f64 is library behaviour, not run
findings.severity: lost write: one transform can leave the document's vector entry undecodable (every later vector command fails; save writes it)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/vector/live_filters.rs:121-145 (transform_live_filters writes m[0]*x + m[2]*y + m[4] etc. with no finite check), called at view/vector/arrange.rs:208 and view/design/auto_layout.rs:1069; arrange.rs:215-224 commit_paths runs entry.validate (paths, styles) and not validate_records; view/vector.rs:754 to_bytes serialises records through serde_json::to_value (non-finite f64 -> null); view/vector.rs:673 decode -> validate_records and serde on every vector_entry(); folio accepts any finite Real (tests/vector_live_filters.rs asserts -1.0e308 Ok); nib admit checks only finiteness when the free distort bounds are unknown
findings.what: Free distort corners are stored as any finite f64. A disabled entry never meets the trial evaluation, because commit_live_filters runs the trial only when an entry is enabled. A layer transform multiplies the corners, and a large stored corner times a scale goes to infinity. It is committed unchecked, written as null, and the next decode of the entry refuses it.
findings.scenario: A loaded document (or update_live_filter on a stack whose only entry is disabled) has a disabled free_distort with src0_h = 1e308. vector.transform_layers {op: scale 200 percent}: src0_h becomes inf, commit_paths commits it, and the entry bytes hold "value": null. The next vector command (vector_entry() -> decode) fails with vector_entry_vector_records, and save writes the broken entry. Undo is the only way back.
findings.fix: Make transform_live_filters return Result<(), String> and refuse the transform typed (for example `{op}: vector_effect_beyond_engine_range`) when a transformed corner is not finite, or exceeds nib's coordinate limit (1e9, which nib refuses at evaluation anyway). Propagate it with `?` at both call sites, before commit. Add one test with a large disabled corner and a scale, expecting a refusal and unchanged entry bytes.

envelope_order_ruling.judgement: The builder's finding is right, and so is its fix. Refusing expand_envelope while the layer holds a live filter is the correct minimal fix. Extend the refusal to any stack on the layer, enabled or disabled.
envelope_order_ruling.spec_basis: The spec fixes no order between an envelope and other live effects. STU-TYP-033 (module 14) calls warp and envelope a StudioEffectStack operation of 14.5 and 14.9. The lane's 'filters, then envelope' is a declared Studio reading (D5, composite DESCRIPTOR and module doc). Two clauses do bind expand. STU-VEC-054 (:4424): expand-appearance MUST 'reproduce the rendered result'. STU-FX-003 (:19397): entries stay enable/disable-able with no quality loss, because each is re-evaluated from the preserved source. expand_envelope as written breaks the first clause whenever an entry is enabled. A disabled entry has no effect at expand time, but re-enabling it later evaluates it over wrapped geometry, which the declared order never produces, so the second clause argues for refusing then as well.
envelope_order_ruling.where: crate hsk-studio-harness-view, crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/vector/envelope.rs:140-177; insert after :147 (the distort_appearance refusal): `if entry.records.live_filter_stack(layer_id).is_some() { return Err("expand_envelope: vector_effect_stack_present (bake or remove the live filters first)".into()); }`. Order evidence: composite src/vector.rs:1489 (stack) before :1521-1544 (envelope).
envelope_order_ruling.fits_lane: Yes. Same crate as live_filters.rs, which the lane already builds; no new crate in the closure (envelope.rs already has every import it needs; live_filter_stack is a folio method already re-exported); no Cargo.toml change. It is the same V4-06 class the lane sweeps (a reader of raw geometry that silently drops or reorders a live filter). It needs the lead's path approval (Q1) and one test: roughen plus warp, then expand_envelope is refused, and the frame and entry bytes are unchanged.
envelope_order_ruling.alternative_rejected: Baking the stack first and then the envelope inside expand_envelope would be expand-appearance over the whole stack (the five expand selectors, STU-VEC-054), which is out of this slice.
